chapter: Virginia school and first Washington bands
title: Summer in Asbury Park with Booker Coleman
summary: The Hot Chocolates played a summer for Reece Dupree in Asbury Park, paid in potatoes and small money, with extra pay on Father Divine nights.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: In fact, the first band I played in was -- big band -- was Booker Coleman -- I mentioned -- and the Hot Chocolates. And he -- we used to go up to Asbury Park and play all the
summer. There was the hall -- a dance hall up there. I forgot the name of it now, but the guy we played for was Reece Dupree and he was out of Philadelphia.

Well, he didn't pay us nothing much. Once he give us a big sack of potatoes and told us to cook them, you know. We all lived in a big house that he rented. It was Marrow's Hall or something like that in Asbury Park.
Was that your pay -- the sack of potatoes?

Yeah. Well, we get a little bit of money once in a while. But then Father Divine used to come in there, and he would -- he would have a big meeting for three or four nights. And the band went right along with the hall, so we'd make about 50-75¢ apiece the nights when he came there. We made pretty good money there because he was drawing a lot of big crowds, you know.
